tables.description: Daily sales fact, one row per date, sku and store. Descriptive attributes live in dim_product and dim_store -- a question about brand, category or region requires a join.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The date of the transaction

columns.name: sku
columns.description: Stock Keeping Unit identifier; joins to dim_product.sku

columns.name: store_id
columns.description: Store identifier; joins to dim_store.store_id. Region and channel are attributes of the store, not of the sale.

columns.name: pack_type
columns.description: Packaging type of the units sold. Stays on the fact rather than dim_product because a single SKU ships in more than one pack type.

columns.name: price_unit
columns.description: Price per unit at the time of sale

columns.name: promotion_flag
columns.description: 1 if sold under promotion, 0 otherwise

columns.name: delivery_days
columns.description: Number of days for delivery

columns.name: stock_available
columns.description: Stock available at the store on that date. A level, not a flow.

columns.name: delivered_qty
columns.description: Quantity delivered to the store

columns.name: units_sold
columns.description: Number of units sold

tables.description: One row per SKU: brand, category, segment, launch date and unit cost.

columns.name: sku
columns.description: Stock Keeping Unit identifier (primary key)

columns.name: brand
columns.description: Brand of the product

columns.name: category
columns.description: Product category

columns.name: segment
columns.description: Market sub-segment within the category

columns.name: launch_date
columns.description: First date the SKU was sold

columns.name: unit_cost
columns.description: Cost of goods per unit, used for margin

tables.description: One row per store: its region, channel, format, city and population tier.

columns.name: store_id
columns.description: Store identifier (primary key)

columns.name: region
columns.description: Geographical region of the store. NOTE: weekly_modeling_data also has a region column; an unqualified reference in a join is ambiguous.

columns.name: channel
columns.description: Sales channel of the store. Also present on weekly_modeling_data.

columns.name: store_format
columns.description: Store format (Hypermarket, Supermarket, Convenience, DiscountStore, FulfilmentCentre)

columns.name: city
columns.description: City the store is in

columns.name: population_tier
columns.description: Catchment size tier (tier_1 largest)

columns.name: opened_date
columns.description: Date the store opened

tables.description: One row per calendar day, covering 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31. The only supported bridge between daily facts and weekly_modeling_data: join fmcg_sales.date to dim_calendar.date, then dim_calendar.week_start to weekly_modeling_data.week.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Calendar day (primary key)

columns.name: week_start
columns.description: Monday of the ISO week this day falls in; equals weekly_modeling_data.week

columns.name: iso_week
columns.description: ISO week number (1-53)

columns.name: year
columns.description: Calendar year

columns.name: month
columns.description: Calendar month (1-12)

columns.name: day_of_week
columns.description: 1 = Monday through 7 = Sunday

columns.name: fiscal_year
columns.description: Fiscal year, which starts on 1 July. Differs from the calendar year for July through December.

columns.name: fiscal_quarter
columns.description: Fiscal quarter 1-4, where Q1 is July to September. Not the same as a calendar quarter.

columns.name: fiscal_week
columns.description: Week number within the fiscal year

columns.name: season
columns.description: Winter, Summer or Shoulder

columns.name: is_holiday
columns.description: True on a public holiday

columns.name: is_holiday_peak
columns.description: True in the pre-Christmas peak trading weeks

tables.description: Daily stock position per store and SKU for the trailing 90 days of the sales period. Carries its own units_sold at the SAME grain as fmcg_sales: summing units_sold from both tables in one query double-counts.

columns.name: date
columns.description: The stock position date

columns.name: store_id
columns.description: Store identifier; joins to dim_store.store_id

columns.name: sku
columns.description: Stock Keeping Unit identifier; joins to dim_product.sku

columns.name: opening_stock
columns.description: Units on hand at the start of the day. A level: summing it across dates is not a quantity.

columns.name: receipts
columns.description: Units received into the store that day

columns.name: units_sold
columns.description: Units sold that day. The same measure fmcg_sales carries, at the same grain.

columns.name: closing_stock
columns.description: Units on hand at the end of the day. A level.

tables.description: One row per promotion period: a date RANGE, not a single date. Joining this to a daily fact on sku alone multiplies every sales row by the number of days in the promotion.

columns.name: promo_id
columns.description: Promotion identifier (primary key)

columns.name: sku
columns.description: The promoted SKU; joins to dim_product.sku

columns.name: region
columns.description: Region the promotion ran in

columns.name: store_id
columns.description: Store the promotion was limited to, or NULL for a chain-wide promotion. An inner join to dim_store drops every chain-wide promotion.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First day of the promotion

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last day of the promotion

columns.name: discount_depth
columns.description: Fractional discount, 0.05 to 0.35

columns.name: mechanic
columns.description: Promotion mechanic (BOGO, PriceOff, Bundle, LoyaltyPoints, DisplayFeature)

tables.description: Aggregated weekly data containing advanced metrics and target variables for predictive modeling. Its grain is the week, not the day: joining it to a daily fact without going through dim_calendar.week_start fans rows out sevenfold.

columns.name: sku
columns.description: Stock Keeping Unit identifier

columns.name: week
columns.description: Monday of the week. Equals dim_calendar.week_start, NOT fmcg_sales.date.

columns.name: channel
columns.description: Sales channel. Also present on dim_store.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Geographical region. Also present on dim_store -- an unqualified reference in a join is ambiguous.

columns.name: units_sold
columns.description: Number of units sold in that week. A weekly total: do not add it to a daily units_sold.

columns.name: stock_available
columns.description: Stock available for that week

columns.name: promotion_flag
columns.description: Whether there was a promotion that week ('True'/'False' or '1'/'0'). NOTE: this is VARCHAR here but INTEGER on fmcg_sales.promotion_flag -- the certified promotional_uplift formula (promotion_flag = 1) is written for fmcg_sales and must not be applied to this column as-is.

columns.name: price_unit
columns.description: Average unit price

columns.name: delivery_days
columns.description: Average delivery days in that week

columns.name: is_holiday_peak
columns.description: Whether it is a peak holiday week ('True'/'False')

columns.name: week_number
columns.description: Week number of the year (1-53)

columns.name: month
columns.description: Month number (1-12)

columns.name: year
columns.description: Year

columns.name: is_holiday_week
columns.description: Whether it is a holiday week ('True'/'False')

columns.name: is_summer
columns.description: Whether it is in the summer season ('True'/'False')

columns.name: is_winter
columns.description: Whether it is in the winter season ('True'/'False')

columns.name: sku_age
columns.description: How long the SKU has been active in weeks

columns.name: lifecycle_stage
columns.description: Product lifecycle stage (e.g., launch, mature, decline)

columns.name: lag_1
columns.description: Units sold in the previous week (lag 1)

columns.name: lag_2
columns.description: Units sold 2 weeks prior (lag 2)

columns.name: rolling_mean_4
columns.description: 4-week rolling average of units sold

columns.name: rolling_std_4
columns.description: 4-week rolling standard deviation of units sold

columns.name: momentum
columns.description: Sales momentum metric

columns.name: target_next_week
columns.description: Target prediction variable for next week's units sold

business_metrics.description: Revenue less cost of goods sold. unit_cost lives on dim_product, so this metric cannot be computed without joining fmcg_sales to dim_product.

business_metrics.definition: (SUM(CASE WHEN promotion_flag = 1 THEN units_sold ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN promotion_flag = 0 THEN units_sold ELSE 0 END)) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN promotion_flag = 0 THEN units_sold ELSE 0 END), 0)
business_metrics.description: The percentage increase in units sold during promotional periods vs non-promotional periods.
The rate at which available stock is being sold.

topic_prompts.prompt:
Your promotion question needs more detail. Would you like to see:

Please re-state with: metric, timeframe, and product/category scope.

suggestions: Compare promotion versus non-promotion units sold by channel.

Which brand had the highest promotional uplift?
What is the stock depletion rate by SKU?

default_recovery_ideas: Compare total revenue across all brands.

few_shot_examples.question: What were total units sold for SKU MI-006 in the PL-South region in the last week of January 2024?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT st.region, st.channel, SUM(s.units_sold) AS total_units_sold
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
JOIN dim_store AS st ON s.store_id = st.store_id
WHERE s.sku = 'MI-006'
  AND st.region = 'PL-South'
  AND s.date BETWEEN '2024-01-22' AND '2024-01-28'
GROUP BY st.region, st.channel
ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Compare total revenue across all brands.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT p.brand,
       ROUND(SUM(s.units_sold * s.price_unit), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
JOIN dim_product AS p ON s.sku = p.sku
GROUP BY p.brand
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Show units sold by category across each sales channel.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT p.category, st.channel,
       SUM(s.units_sold) AS total_units
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
JOIN dim_product AS p ON s.sku = p.sku
JOIN dim_store AS st ON s.store_id = st.store_id
GROUP BY p.category, st.channel
ORDER BY p.category, total_units DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Compare units sold during promotion versus non-promotion periods by channel.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT st.channel, s.promotion_flag,
       SUM(s.units_sold) AS total_units,
       ROUND(SUM(s.units_sold * s.price_unit), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
JOIN dim_store AS st ON s.store_id = st.store_id
GROUP BY st.channel, s.promotion_flag
ORDER BY st.channel, s.promotion_flag

few_shot_examples.question: What is the stock depletion rate by category?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT p.category,
       ROUND(SUM(s.units_sold) * 1.0 / NULLIF(SUM(s.stock_available), 0), 4) AS stock_depletion_rate,
       SUM(s.stock_available) AS total_stock,
       SUM(s.units_sold) AS total_units_sold
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
JOIN dim_product AS p ON s.sku = p.sku
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY stock_depletion_rate DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Which brand had the highest week-on-week growth in units sold in 2024?
few_shot_examples.sql:
WITH weekly AS (
    SELECT p.brand,
           DATE_TRUNC('week', CAST(s.date AS DATE)) AS week_start,
           SUM(s.units_sold) AS units
    FROM fmcg_sales AS s
    JOIN dim_product AS p ON s.sku = p.sku
    WHERE s.date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-12-31'
    GROUP BY p.brand, DATE_TRUNC('week', CAST(s.date AS DATE))
),
growth AS (
    SELECT brand, week_start, units,
           LAG(units) OVER (PARTITION BY brand ORDER BY week_start) AS prev_units
    FROM weekly
)
SELECT brand, week_start, units, prev_units,
       (units - prev_units) AS wow_change
FROM growth
WHERE prev_units IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY wow_change DESC
LIMIT 10

few_shot_examples.question: Show total revenue year over year.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.date AS DATE)) AS year,
       ROUND(SUM(s.units_sold * s.price_unit), 2) AS total_revenue,
       SUM(s.units_sold) AS total_units
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year

few_shot_examples.question: Compare revenue by pack type across categories.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT s.pack_type, p.category,
       ROUND(SUM(s.units_sold * s.price_unit), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
JOIN dim_product AS p ON s.sku = p.sku
GROUP BY s.pack_type, p.category
ORDER BY s.pack_type, total_revenue DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Show monthly revenue trend by channel.
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT st.channel,
       DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST(s.date AS DATE)) AS month_start,
       ROUND(SUM(s.units_sold * s.price_unit), 2) AS total_revenue
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
JOIN dim_store AS st ON s.store_id = st.store_id
GROUP BY st.channel, DATE_TRUNC('month', CAST(s.date AS DATE))
ORDER BY month_start, total_revenue DESC

few_shot_examples.question: Which category had the highest promotional uplift?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT p.category,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.promotion_flag = 1 THEN s.units_sold ELSE 0 END) AS promo_units,
       SUM(CASE WHEN s.promotion_flag = 0 THEN s.units_sold ELSE 0 END) AS non_promo_units,
       ROUND(
           (
               SUM(CASE WHEN s.promotion_flag = 1 THEN s.units_sold ELSE 0 END)
               - SUM(CASE WHEN s.promotion_flag = 0 THEN s.units_sold ELSE 0 END)
           ) * 1.0
           / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN s.promotion_flag = 0 THEN s.units_sold ELSE 0 END), 0),
           4
       ) AS promotional_uplift_rate
FROM fmcg_sales AS s
JOIN dim_product AS p ON s.sku = p.sku
GROUP BY p.category
ORDER BY promotional_uplift_rate DESC

few_shot_examples.question: What is the average units sold by lifecycle stage?
few_shot_examples.sql:
SELECT lifecycle_stage,
       ROUND(AVG(units_sold), 2) AS avg_units_sold
FROM weekly_modeling_data
GROUP BY lifecycle_stage
ORDER BY avg_units_sold DESC

row_policies.name: region_scope
row_policies.description: A regional analyst reads only the stores in the regions they are granted. Every table that can attribute a row to a store is scoped: the ones carrying region filter on it directly, the ones carrying only store_id are scoped through dim_store, so the restriction holds whether or not the query joined the dimension.
